title: Central Star Pressing Structure
definition: A defensive formation where a compact central block forces opponents wide, triggering a one-sided overload to recover possession.
content: This tactical concept involves arranging the front line and midfield pivots in a narrow, star-like shape to dominate the central channels. By creating a numerical superiority in the center, the team blocks direct central progression. When the opposition is forced to play wide, the nearest wing-back immediately presses the ball carrier, while the central players cover passing lanes and the far-side center-back tracks the wide option. This creates a localized overload that forces the opponent to retreat or switch play. If the press is broken, the team transitions into a 5-4-1 low block, using inverted forwards as wide midfielders to shield the center. Crucially, upon winning the ball back, the team may intentionally invite a counter-press to draw opponents forward before launching long balls to isolated forwards. This approach relies on specific player roles, such as versatile full-backs who can invert or overlap, and box-to-box midfielders who drop deep for build-up but advance between lines in attack. The strategy prioritizes spatial control and psychological manipulation over immediate counter-attacks.
